html:
On 8 August 1956 a fire in the Bois du Cazier coal mine at Marcinelle, near Charleroi, killed 262 miners. It was the worst mining disaster in Belgian history.

More than half the dead were Italians. After the Second World War Belgium needed coal and miners, and in 1946 Italy agreed to send workers in return for coal. Tens of thousands of Italians came to the mines of Wallonia, living in former prisoner camps.

After the disaster Italy stopped sending miners, and Belgium turned to workers from Spain, Greece, Morocco and Turkey, the start of its later immigrant communities. Coal mining in Wallonia soon went into decline, part of the decline of heavy industry that followed the coal and steel community. The mine is now a memorial and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. See Belgium and the Italian diaspora.
